newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland restores power as snow continues.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland restores power as snow continues.

text.p: Centerior Energy Corp unit Cleveland Electric Illuminating Co was working Monday to restore power to about 62,000 customers after a freak early snowstorm hit the area this weekend, a spokesman said.
"It's the earliest and worst November storm we've seen in three decades," company spokesman Jim Sielicki said Monday.
About 157,000 customers in northeast Ohio lost power after 12 to 15 inches of heavy, wet snow Saturday night and early Sunday knocked down trees and power lines.
The heavy snow continued in the area, with another 10 inches of snow expected Monday, Sielicki said.
Although power had been restored to about 92,000 customers, the majority of areas remaining without power may not have electricity until Wednesday, the spokesman said.
Repair efforts were being hampered by continued snow he said, adding, "trying to get the (repair) trucks through the snow is a real problem."
Over 300 crews were working to clear fallen trees and reach downed power lines, he said.
In addition to Cleveland Electric's repair staff, crews had been sent to help from Centerior subsidiary Toledo Edison Co, Ohio Edison Co and American Electric Power Co Inc, he said.
While more than 800 power lines were damaged, a total of 32 main electricity feeder lines were also damaged by the storm, Sielicki said.
